factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua

about: A Padilla blend built on Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan Corojo 99, sold direct through the Padilla website in four sizes.
notes: The maker does not publish the binder, factory, strength or tasting notes.

about: The maduro version of Padilla's Artefacto, pairing a Mexican San Andres wrapper with Nicaraguan fillers that include Aganorsa Corojo. It is sold direct through the Padilla website.
notes: The maker does not publish the binder, factory or strength. Padilla says it is made in batches and was out of stock for nearly two years while one filler leaf was unavailable.

about: Padilla's best-known cigar, rolled in small batches at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana. It is named for the corner of 8th Street and 11th Avenue, where the original 2005 version was made by Pepin Garcia.
notes: The blend and factory have changed several times since 2005; the current El Titan de Bronze version dates to 2020. The maker lists an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper, while halfwheel and Neptune list a Nicaraguan wrapper. Neptune's description calls it medium to full.

about: The San Andres maduro counterpart to the Padilla Miami, with aged Nicaraguan fillers. It was introduced in 2012 as a small-batch cigar rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami.
notes: Launched in 2012 at El Titan de Bronze in Miami. Padilla's main listing still says it is rolled in Miami, but another Padilla listing says the blend was reworked in Nicaragua, so check where current stock is made before quoting it.

about: A lighter-wrapped edition of the Padilla Miami, keeping the same filler blend under a Habano Claro wrapper. It is rolled in very small batches at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana.
notes: The maker describes it as slightly milder than the regular Miami and calls it an extremely limited release. The wrapper's country of origin and the binder are not published.

about: Factory seconds of the regular Padilla Miami, rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami and sold at a discount. The maker says they were set aside only because the wrapper color varied.
notes: Same cigar as the regular Padilla Miami with slight wrapper color variation, aged more than a year, per the maker. A one-time batch sold in 5-packs; the listing gives no size or blend details.

factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua

about: A small-batch Padilla maduro first released in 2013 and brought back in 2025 as Vintage Reserve 3.0. The current version uses aged Nicaraguan fillers from Esteli and Jalapa under a dark maduro wrapper.
notes: The 2013 original was made by Oliva in Nicaragua with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper in Robusto, Torpedo and Churchill, as a numbered limited run. For the current 3.0 pre-release the maker does not name the wrapper leaf, binder, factory or size.

about: Padilla's first line, built around a golden hybrid-seed wrapper from the grower ASP that the maker likens to Connecticut smoothness with Habano bite. It was reintroduced in 2025 as a limited run of Toros sold direct.

about: A small-batch Padilla blend built around tobacco from Ometepe, the volcanic island in Lake Nicaragua. It is sold direct from Padilla in 5-packs of Robustos.
